name: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; earned a PhD in physics at 24 (1976) but his Nobel Prize-winning ribosome work came decades later (2000s).
early_history_summary: Born in Chidambaram, India to biochemist parents; grew up in Baroda. Earned B.Sc. in physics from Baroda University (1971) and PhD in physics from Ohio University (1976), then switched to biology at UCSD. His landmark ribosome structure work occurred at Brookhaven and Cambridge in the 1990s-2000s.
family_context_summary: Born to two biochemists; father headed biochemistry department at M.S. University of Baroda. Parents did postdoctoral work in the US and Canada.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father C.V. Ramakrishnan was a biochemist who headed a university department; mother R. Rajalakshmi also taught biochemistry. Strong scientific household.
evidence_summary: Ramakrishnan earned a PhD in physics by age 24 but had no independently notable scientific achievement by 26. His Nobel Prize-winning work on ribosome structure came in the 2000s, decades after age 26. A PhD is a standard credential, not a material milestone in the sense of this project.

name: Hillel Furstenberg
milestone_by_age_26: Published 'On the infinitude of primes' in the American Mathematical Monthly (1955) at age 20, providing a novel topological proof of Euclid's theorem while an undergraduate at Yeshiva University.
early_history_summary: Born in Berlin to a Jewish family in 1935; escaped Nazi Germany in 1939 after Kristallnacht, settling in New York City. His father died on the journey; he was raised by his mother (a sewing machine operator) and older sister who tutored him in math. He showed early mathematical promise, attended Yeshiva University, and published multiple papers as an undergraduate, including his famous topological proof of the infinitude of primes at age 20.
family_context_summary: Born into a Jewish family in Nazi Germany; father died during escape to the US in 1939. Raised in financial hardship by his mother, a sewing machine operator, in Washington Heights, New York.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of parental mathematical expertise; his sister, three years older, served as his early math tutor, keeping him ahead of his class.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Holocaust survivor, financial hardship, sister tutoring, Yeshiva University, early publication
evidence_summary: Furstenberg escaped Nazi Germany as a child, lost his father, and grew up in financial hardship in New York. His older sister tutored him in mathematics, keeping him ahead of his peers. He attended Yeshiva University where he published several papers as an undergraduate, including his famous topological proof of the infinitude of primes in the American Mathematical Monthly at age 20. He then earned his PhD from Princeton under Salomon Bochner at age 23. The adversity of his childhood and his sister's early tutoring appear to have been key catalysts.
starting_point: Born in 1935 in Berlin to a Jewish family; father died during escape from Nazi Germany in 1939; raised in financial hardship by his mother, a sewing machine operator, in New York City.
current_position: Professor emeritus at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem; retired in 2003; co-recipient of the 2020 Abel Prize and the Wolf Prize in Mathematics.

trajectory.event: Published 'On the infinitude of primes' in the American Mathematical Monthly while an undergraduate at Yeshiva University.
Received PhD in mathematics from Princeton University under Salomon Bochner with thesis 'Prediction Theory'.
Moved to the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, where he spent the rest of his academic career.
Awarded the Wolf Prize in Mathematics.
Co-awarded the Abel Prize with Gregory Margulis for pioneering methods from probability and dynamics in group theory, number theory and combinatorics.

name: Danijel Šarić
milestone_by_age_26: Won two consecutive national championships with Crvena zvezda (Red Star Belgrade) in 1997 and 1998 as a starting goalkeeper, beginning at age 20.
early_history_summary: Born in Doboj, Bosnia (then Yugoslavia), Šarić began his handball career at hometown club Sloga Doboj before moving to Borac Banja Luka. He joined Crvena zvezda (Red Star Belgrade) in 1996 at age 19 and won two consecutive Yugoslav national championships in 1997 and 1998. He later had a long international career in Spain and Qatar, including seven seasons at FC Barcelona.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yugoslav handball tradition, Red Star Belgrade, youth clubs, physical stature
evidence_summary: Šarić grew up in the Yugoslav handball tradition, starting at hometown club Sloga Doboj and then Borac Banja Luka before joining Crvena zvezda at 19. He won two national championships there at ages 20-21. His 1.94m frame was well-suited for goalkeeping. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources. The Yugoslav/Serbian handball pipeline provided direct access to elite-level competition from a young age.
starting_point: Born in 1977 in Doboj, Bosnia (then SFR Yugoslavia); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Playing for Al Arabi in Qatar as of 2025; had a long career including seven seasons at FC Barcelona (2009-2016) and representing Qatar internationally.

trajectory.event: Won the Yugoslav national championship with Crvena zvezda (Red Star Belgrade) as goalkeeper.
Won a second consecutive national championship with Crvena zvezda.
Joined FC Barcelona, beginning a seven-season tenure at one of Europe's top handball clubs.
Won silver medal at the World Handball Championship representing Qatar.
Represented Qatar at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

name: Levente Lengyel
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; gained the International Master title in 1962 at age 29 and the Grandmaster title in 1964 at age 31. His first Chess Olympiad was in 1960 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Born in Debrecen, Hungary in 1933. Little is documented about his early chess career before his first Olympiad appearance in 1960 at age 27. He gained the International Master title in 1962 and Grandmaster title in 1964.
evidence_summary: Lengyel's first documented international chess achievement was playing in the 1960 Chess Olympiad at age 27. His International Master title came in 1962 (age 29) and Grandmaster title in 1964 (age 31). No evidence of a material milestone by age 26 was found in reviewed sources.

name: Bernhard Schlink
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; graduated law school at 24 (1968) but his literary career began with his first detective novel at age 43 (1987) and The Reader was published at age 51 (1995).
early_history_summary: Born in 1944 near Bielefeld, Germany, the son of theology professor Edmund Schlink. Grew up in Heidelberg, studied law at Heidelberg and the Free University of Berlin, graduating in 1968. Earned his doctorate in 1975 and became a law professor in 1982. His literary career began late, with his first novel published in 1987.
family_context_summary: Son of Edmund Schlink, a prominent Lutheran theology professor at Heidelberg University. Mother was Swiss. Grew up in an academic household in Heidelberg.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a famous Lutheran theologian and professor at Heidelberg University; not a literary or legal domain, but provided an academic environment.
evidence_summary: Schlink studied law and graduated at 24, but his literary fame arrived at 51 with The Reader (1995). His first novel was published at 43. No material literary or legal milestone by age 26 was found; a law degree is a standard credential.

name: Takashi Murakami
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; earned BFA at 24 (1986) and MFA at 26 (1988) from Tokyo University of the Arts, but his first solo show was in 1989 at age 27 and his signature Superflat movement and Mr. DOB character emerged in the mid-1990s.
early_history_summary: Born in Tokyo in 1962 to a taxi driver father and homemaker mother who studied needlepoint and textile design. Initially wanted to be an animator, attended Tokyo University of the Arts, majoring in Nihonga (traditional Japanese painting). Earned BFA (1986), MFA (1988), and PhD (1993). His first solo show was in 1989 at Tokyo's Ginza Surugadai Gallery.
family_context_summary: Father was a taxi driver; mother was a homemaker who studied needlepoint and textile design. Mother had influence on Murakami's interest in the arts and required him to write reviews of exhibitions he visited.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother studied needlepoint and textile design, exposing Murakami to art from childhood, but no direct professional art-world connection is documented.
evidence_summary: Murakami earned his MFA at 26 but had no notable exhibition or artistic breakthrough by that age. His first solo show came at 27 (1989), and his career-defining Superflat movement and Mr. DOB character emerged in the mid-1990s. Academic degrees are standard credentials, not material milestones.

name: Denise Scott Brown
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; earned her architectural degree from the AA in London at 24 (1955) but her influential work with Robert Venturi, including Learning from Las Vegas, came in the late 1960s-1970s.
early_history_summary: Born in 1931 in Nkana, Northern Rhodesia (now Zambia) to Jewish parents from Eastern Europe. Grew up in Johannesburg from age two. Wanted to be an architect from age five. Studied at the University of the Witwatersrand (1948-52), then the Architectural Association in London (degree 1955). Married Robert Scott Brown in 1955; he died in 1959. She then earned a Master's in City Planning at Penn (1958-60).
family_context_summary: Born to Jewish parents from Eastern Europe who emigrated to southern Africa. Father was an entrepreneur involved in trading, stockbroking, and film distribution in Johannesburg. Mother grew up in rural Southern Rhodesia.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an entrepreneur in Johannesburg with international business connections; not an architecture domain, but provided exposure to international visitors and multicultural environment.
evidence_summary: Scott Brown earned her AA architectural degree at 24 but had no built work, major publication, or professional recognition by age 26. Her influential career with Robert Venturi, including Learning from Las Vegas (1972), came well after age 26. An architectural degree is a standard professional credential.

name: Denis Mukwege
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; earned his medical degree from the University of Burundi in 1983 at age 28. His founding of Panzi Hospital came in 1999 and the Nobel Peace Prize in 2018.
early_history_summary: Born in 1955 in Bukavu, Belgian Congo (now DRC), the third of nine children of a Pentecostal pastor. Accompanied his father on visits to the sick, inspiring him to become a doctor. Earned medical degree from University of Burundi in 1983, then specialized in gynecology at University of Angers, France (1989). Founded Panzi Hospital in 1999.
family_context_summary: Born to a Pentecostal pastor father and his wife in Bukavu, DRC. Third of nine children. Father's pastoral work visiting the sick inspired Mukwege's medical calling.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Pentecostal pastor; no medical or scientific domain expertise in the family is documented.
evidence_summary: Mukwege did not complete his medical degree until age 28 (1983). His landmark achievement, founding Panzi Hospital, came at age 44 (1999), and the Nobel Peace Prize at 63 (2018). No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Phạm Tuân
milestone_by_age_26: Credited with shooting down a US B-52 Stratofortress bomber on the night of December 27, 1972 during Operation Linebacker II, and awarded the title Hero of the People's Armed Forces in 1973, at age 25-26.
early_history_summary: Born in 1947 in Kiến Xương, Thái Bình province, North Vietnam, to a farming family. Joined the military in 1965 as a radar mechanic student, was selected for pilot training, and graduated from Krasnodar Flight School in the Soviet Union as a MiG-17 pilot in 1967 at age 20. Became a combat fighter pilot in the Vietnam War, developing night interception techniques against US air raids. On December 27, 1972, he engaged B-52 bombers in his MiG-21MF and was credited with downing one, becoming the first Vietnamese pilot to shoot down a B-52 in air-to-air combat.
family_context_summary: Born to a farming family in rural North Vietnam. No documented family connections to aviation or military leadership.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Vietnam War, farming family, Soviet pilot training, combat experience, night interception
evidence_summary: Phạm Tuân came from a farming family in rural North Vietnam with no documented advantages. He was recruited into the air force at 18, trained as a pilot in the Soviet Union, and graduated at 20. Through years of combat experience during the Vietnam War, he developed rare night interception skills. At 25, he was credited with shooting down a B-52 bomber during Operation Linebacker II, earning the Hero of the People's Armed Forces title. The wartime context and Soviet training pipeline were the primary accelerants of his early career.
starting_point: Born in 1947 in Kiến Xương, Thái Bình province, North Vietnam, to a farming family with no documented military or aviation connections.
current_position: Retired Lieutenant General of the Vietnam People's Air Force; lives in Hanoi; formerly Chairman of the General Department for Defense Industry. First Asian person in space (Soyuz 37, 1980).

trajectory.event: Graduated from Krasnodar Flight School in the Soviet Union as a MiG-17 pilot and returned to North Vietnam.
Credited with shooting down a US B-52 Stratofortress during Operation Linebacker II on the night of December 27, the first Vietnamese pilot to achieve this in air-to-air combat.
Awarded the title Hero of the People's Armed Forces for his combat service.
Became the first Vietnamese and first Asian person in space aboard Soyuz 37 as an Interkosmos research cosmonaut.
Retired from the Vietnam People's Air Force with the rank of Lieutenant General.

name: Grzegorz Lato
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal with Poland at the 1972 Munich Olympics at age 22, having already debuted for the Polish national team at 21 and played professionally at Stal Mielec from age 16.
early_history_summary: Born in 1950 in Malbork, Poland. Began his senior career at Stal Mielec in 1966 at age 16, where he spent 14 seasons. Made his international debut for Poland in 1971 at age 21. Won Olympic gold at the 1972 Munich Olympics, and later was the top scorer at the 1974 FIFA World Cup with seven goals.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Grew up in Malbork, Poland during the communist era.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stal Mielec, Polish football system, early professional debut, national team
evidence_summary: Lato began his professional career at Stal Mielec at 16, benefiting from the Polish football system's talent pipeline. By 21 he was in the national team, and at 22 he won Olympic gold at Munich. Family background is not documented. The Polish football infrastructure and his early entry into professional play were the key accelerants. He later became top scorer at the 1974 World Cup.
starting_point: Born in 1950 in Malbork, Poland; family background not documented in reviewed sources; grew up in communist-era Poland.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 1984; later served as Senator of Poland (2001-2005) and President of the Polish Football Association (PZPN, 2008-2012).

trajectory.event: Began senior professional career at Stal Mielec, where he would play for 14 seasons.
Made his international debut for the Polish national team against West Germany.
Won Olympic gold medal with Poland at the Munich Summer Olympics.
Finished as top scorer at the 1974 FIFA World Cup with seven goals, helping Poland to third place.
Won Olympic silver medal with Poland at the Montreal Summer Olympics.
Moved abroad to join Lokeren in Belgium, his first club outside Poland.

name: Tony Hoare
milestone_by_age_26: Invented the Quicksort algorithm while a graduate student at Moscow State University in 1959-1960, at age 25-26, one of the most widely used sorting algorithms in computer science.
early_history_summary: Born in 1934 in Colombo, Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) to parents in the British colonial administration. Educated at the Dragon School in Oxford and King's School in Canterbury, then studied classics and philosophy at Merton College, Oxford (graduated 1956). Served in the Royal Navy (1956-58) studying Russian. Returned to Oxford for statistics, then went to Moscow State University (1959-60) to study machine translation under Kolmogorov, where he invented Quicksort. Joined Elliott Brothers in 1960, led the ALGOL 60 compiler team, and became Professor at Queen's University Belfast in 1968.
family_context_summary: Born to parents involved in the British colonial administration in Ceylon. Received elite English education at the Dragon School in Oxford and King's School in Canterbury.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were in the British colonial administration; no direct computing or mathematical domain expertise documented, but the family provided access to elite English schooling.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Dragon School, Merton College Oxford, Moscow State University, Kolmogorov, ALGOL 60, Quicksort
evidence_summary: Hoare benefited from an elite British education (Dragon School, King's School Canterbury, Merton College Oxford) through his family's colonial administration background. He studied classics and philosophy, then pivoted to computing via statistics and a graduate stint at Moscow State University under Kolmogorov. There, while working on machine translation at age 25-26, he invented Quicksort, one of the most important algorithms in computing. His access to elite institutions on both sides of the Cold War divide was unusual and directly catalyzed his breakthrough.
starting_point: Born in 1934 in Colombo, Ceylon to parents in the British colonial administration; received elite education at the Dragon School in Oxford and King's School in Canterbury.
current_position: Died on March 5, 2026 at age 92; final roles were Emeritus Professor at Oxford University and Senior Researcher at Microsoft Research Cambridge.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Merton College, Oxford with a degree in classics and philosophy (Greats).
Went to Moscow State University as a British Council exchange student to study machine translation under Andrey Kolmogorov.
Invented the Quicksort algorithm while at Moscow State University, originally to sort Russian words for dictionary lookup in machine translation.
Joined Elliott Brothers in the UK, leading the team that produced the first commercial ALGOL 60 compiler.
Appointed Professor of Computing Science at Queen's University Belfast, where he built a strong research department.
Received the ACM A.M. Turing Award for fundamental contributions to programming language definition and design.
Died on March 5, 2026 in Cambridge, UK.

name: Henrique Mecking
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Brazilian Chess Championship at age 13 in 1965, becoming the youngest national champion in history; won the South American Zonal at 15 (1967) becoming an International Master, and became Brazil's first Grandmaster at 20 (1972).
early_history_summary: Born in 1952 in Santa Cruz do Sul, Brazil to a bank clerk father and a mother who taught him chess at age six using a checkers/chess board. Won his state championship at 11, the Brazilian Championship at 13 (youngest ever), and the South American Zonal at 15, earning the International Master title. Became Brazil's first Grandmaster in 1972 at age 20, and won the Petrópolis Interzonal in 1973. Reached world #3 ranking in 1978 before illness (myasthenia gravis) interrupted his career.
family_context_summary: Father was a bank clerk at Banco do Brasil who moved frequently for work. Mother bought a checkers/chess board and taught Henrique chess at age six. Middle-class family in southern Brazil.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother introduced chess to Henrique at age six using a dual checkers/chess board; she had learned the game herself and taught him. No documented professional chess background in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chess prodigy, mother taught chess, Brazilian championship at 13, IM at 15, Fischer comparisons
evidence_summary: Mecking was a self-evident chess prodigy: taught by his mother at six, winning his state championship at 11, and the Brazilian national championship at 13, the youngest ever. His mother's introduction of chess was the key early catalyst, but no dedicated coach or elite training infrastructure is documented. He became an International Master at 15 and Brazil's first Grandmaster at 20, despite Brazil having minimal chess tradition. His career was later disrupted by myasthenia gravis at age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Santa Cruz do Sul, Brazil to a bank clerk father at Banco do Brasil and a mother who taught him chess at age six; middle-class family in southern Brazil.
current_position: Still active as a chess player in Brazil with a FIDE rating around 2553; known as Mequinho, Brazil's greatest chess player; deeply religious since recovering from myasthenia gravis.

trajectory.event: Won the Brazilian Chess Championship, becoming the youngest national champion in history.
Won the South American Zonal Tournament, earning the International Master title as the youngest IM at the time.
Became Brazil's first chess Grandmaster, awarded by FIDE.
Won the Petrópolis Interzonal tournament, qualifying for the Candidates matches for the World Chess Championship.
Reached world #3 ranking, behind only World Champion Anatoly Karpov and Viktor Korchnoi, before illness interrupted his career.
Returned to competitive chess after recovering from myasthenia gravis.
